info.title: Napta Integration API
info.description: This API documentation uses example data. For documentation specific to your Napta instance, visit the app's admin page.

tags.name: Introduction
tags.description:
This documentation shows how to use the integration API.

Why "integration"? Because this API is mainly intended to be used for the integration of Napta with your Information System:
- to import data from your Information System to Napta
- to export data from Napta to your Information System


The base URL for this API is `https://api.napta.io/integration/v1`.
`https://api.napta.io/integration/v0` is a deprecated alias of the very same API: both base URLs expose the
exact same endpoints and the exact same behaviour. `v0` is still supported for backward compatibility, but it
should no longer be used: `v1` is the recommended base URL.


URLs and data sent to this API should be UTF-8 encoded. Body of requests must be valid JSON objects. Float values only accept dot character as decimal separator.


To be provided with access and use this API, ask credentials to your Napta Contact.


Naming conventions used in this documentation correspond to the English version of your Napta app.
To align with the documentation,
you can switch to the English language by accessing the language selector located under your profile picture in the top right corner of the app interface.


This API is neither restricted by rights configured on the App nor by rights of the user to whom the credentials are linked.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
This API authenticates requests using **OAuth2 Bearer tokens**.


To obtain a token, use the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow —
set the `audience` parameter to `integration` to scope the token to this API.
The access token is valid for **2 hours** and should be reused as long as it is valid.
You may experience limitations if you request more than **200 tokens** per day.


```cURL
curl --request POST \   
    --url 'https://login.napta.io/oauth/token' \        
    --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \        
    --data grant_type=client_credentials \      
    --data client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \   
    --data client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \   
    --data audience=integration
```

Reminder: Ask your Napta Contact for a `client_id` and `client_secret`.

Once you have an access token, pass it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header:

```cURL
curl --request GET \    
    --url 'https://api.napta.io/integration/v1/users' \         
    --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN'
```
For more information about obtaining tokens, please refer to
[OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow](https://oauth.net/2/grant-types/client-credentials/).

tags.name: Rate limiting and performance
tags.description:
## Overview

The Integration API enforces rate limits to ensure fair usage and system stability. You have three configurable rate limits:

### Default Limits
- **10 seconds:** 100 requests (moving/rolling window)
- **Daily:** 50,000 requests (fixed 24-hour window)
- **Monthly:** 750,000 requests (fixed 30-day window)

> These are default values. Your organization may have custom limits configured.

### How Rate Limit Windows Work

**10-Second Moving Window (Rolling):**
- Continuously tracks requests over any rolling 10-second period
- Each request counts against your limit for exactly 10 seconds
- As time passes, old requests expire and your available count increases

*Example:* You start with 100 requests available.
- 14:30:00: Make 1 request → 99 available
- 14:30:01: Make 1 request → 98 available
- 14:30:10: First request expires (10 seconds old) → 99 available
- 14:30:11: Second request expires → 100 available

Think of it as a sliding 10-second window: each request "uses a slot" for 10 seconds, then automatically frees it up.

**Daily Fixed Window (24 hours from first request):**
- NOT a calendar day (midnight to midnight)
- Your 24-hour window starts with your first request
- You have up to 50,000 requests to use during this 24-hour period
- Only resets when the full 24 hours expire
- After reset, a new window only starts when you make your next request

*Example:* You start with 50,000 requests available.
- March 28, 16:43:00: Make your first request → 49,999 available, window starts
- March 28, 20:00:00: Used 30,000 requests → 20,000 available
- March 29, 00:00:00: Used all 50,000 → 0 available (still in same window!)
- March 29, 16:42:59: Still 0 available (window hasn't expired yet)
- March 29, 16:43:00: Window expires, no active window
- March 30, 09:15:00: Make a request → 49,999 available, new 24-hour window starts

Think of it as a 24-hour timer that starts when you make your first request. You get one bucket of 50,000 requests to use during those 24 hours. When the timer expires, no new timer starts until you make another request.

**Monthly Fixed Window (30 days from first request):**
- NOT a calendar month (January, February, etc.)
- Your 30-day window starts with your first request
- You have up to 750,000 requests to use during this 30-day period
- Only resets when the full 30 days expire
- After reset, a new window only starts when you make your next request

*Example:* You start with 750,000 requests available.
- March 28, 16:43:00: Make your first request → 749,999 available, window starts
- April 15: Used 500,000 requests → 250,000 available
- April 27, 16:42:59: Used all 750,000 → 0 available (still in same window!)
- April 27, 16:43:00: Window expires, no active window
- May 2, 10:30:00: Make a request → 749,999 available, new 30-day window starts

Think of it as a 30-day timer that starts when you make your first request. You get one bucket of 750,000 requests to use during those 30 days. When the timer expires, no new timer starts until you make another request.

### Rate Limit Errors

When you exceed a limit, you'll receive:
- **Status Code:** `429 Too Many Requests`
- **Error Message:** Indicates which limit was exceeded
  - 10-second: "Too many requests in a short period. Please slow down and try again in a few seconds."
  - Daily: "Daily quota exceeded. Contact support if you need a higher limit."
  - Monthly: "Monthly quota exceeded. Contact support if you need a higher limit."

### Best Practices

**Handle 429 Errors:**
- Implement exponential backoff (wait 1s, then 2s, 4s, 8s...)
- For 10-second limits: retry after a few seconds
- For daily/monthly limits: wait for window reset or contact support

### Requesting Higher Limits

If you consistently hit rate limits, contact your Napta sales representative to discuss increasing your limits.

tags.name: Error management
tags.description:
Handle errors gracefully, especially with exponential backoff:

**429 (Too Many Requests)**
Indicates that you've exceeded your rate limits. If you breach the 10-second moving window, retrying with exponential backoff is recommended.
If you surpass daily or monthly thresholds, you'll likely need to contact Napta sales to raise these limits.
Note that 429 errors do not count against your rate limits. Because the API is idempotent, you can safely retry failed requests.

**5xx (Server Errors)**
These errors can occur during auto-scaling or deployment. Retry with exponential backoff until the system becomes stable.
If the error persists it's likely a bug in the API. In this case, please report it to Napta support with the request details.

Since this API is idempotent, repeated calls on errors do not cause data corruption.

tags.name: External Ids
tags.description:
Some objects (such as Project, User and Assignment) have an external_id field.

This field is empty by default and can be used to store a **unique reference** to the object in your system.


For example, if you have a project with an id : `PROJECT-007` in your system, you can set the external_id of the
corresponding project in Napta to `PROJECT-007`.


This allows you to easily retrieve / update the corresponding object in Napta by using the external_id field directly
**instead of having to maintain an association table between your ids and Napta ids**.
External IDs are **case sensitive** when matching: for example, `PROJECT-007` is not equivalent to `Project-007`.

In our system, External IDs are uniquely assigned, with the exception of the `null` value,
which can be associated with multiple objects.
This `null` value is allowed wherever the External IDs field is applicable.

The external_id field may be updated by providing both the Napta ID and the external ID in the request.

The Napta ID will be used to identify the object to update, and the external ID will be updated.

Providing an external_id with the `null` value will remove the external ID from the object.

tags.name: Create vs Update behavior
tags.description:
The PUT method is used to create or update a resource.

⚠️ Unlike standard REST conventions, this API uses PUT with partial update semantics.

On creation (when the resource does not exist):
- Any omitted fields will be set to their default values.
- Required fields must be provided.

On update (when the resource already exists):
- Only the fields explicitly provided in the request body will be updated.
- Omitted fields will be left unchanged.
- This allows you to update specific fields without resending the full resource.
However, required fields must still be included, even if their values are not being changed.

tags.name: Pagination
tags.description:
Several endpoints of this API employ pagination,
making it essential to include pagination parameters in your request.
For your initial query, simply specify the 'limit' parameter.
For any subsequent queries, you must include the 'cursor' parameter,
which you will receive in the prior response as 'next_cursor'.

Pagination uses a cursor-based approach, ensuring reliable data retrieval even during deletions or insertions.
This method prevents missing or duplicating entries while paginating through the data.

tags.name: Custom Fields
tags.description:
Several endpoints of this API expose `custom_text_fields` and `custom_dropdown_fields` fields to enable the storage of additional information.


## Custom Text Fields
Custom text fields can be created and managed through the Napta App [here](https://app.napta.io/admin/metadata_field).


Once created, these fields dynamically appear in the API documentation and can be used to store text information.

These fields may also be referred as `metadata`.

## Custom Dropdown Fields
Custom dropdown fields can be created and managed through the Napta App [here](https://app.napta.io/admin/tag_type).


Important Notes:

- Once created, these fields must have a "key" to dynamically appear in the API documentation and can be used to store information as a dropdown.
- Dropdown values are created when specified in the request but are not deleted when no longer used.
- Dropdown values given as an identifier (instead of a name) must already exist in your referential, otherwise the request will fail.
- Single select dropdown must be given a string. Multi select dropdown must be given a list of string.

These fields may also be referred as `tags`.

tags.name: Translated Fields
tags.description:
Some fields in this API are multilingual, allowing you to store and retrieve content in different languages.

## Supported Languages
The following language codes are currently supported: **en** (English), **fr** (French), **de** (German) and **it** (Italian).


## Creation and Initial Assignment
When creating an object or assigning a value to a field that was previously `null`, **you must ensure every supported language receives a value.** To achieve this, you have two options:
- **Explicitly provide** a translation for every single supported language code.
- **Use the `default_translation` key** to automatically fill any language not explicitly specified in your request.

## Updates
For updates to existing values, you can perform partial updates:
- Only include the specific language keys you wish to modify.
- Languages omitted from the request will remain unchanged.
- The `default_translation` key is **strictly ignored** during updates.

## Default Translation
The `default_translation` key is a "write-only" helper. It is used only during the processing of your request to populate the supported languages and is **not stored** in the application. It will never appear in the API responses.

Even if you provide values for all currently supported languages, we recommend always including a `default_translation`. This ensures your objects remain fully populated and valid if the application introduces support for additional languages in the future.

## Example Request
If you only want to provide the English and French versions and let the system handle the rest during creation:

```json
"description": {
    "en": "Description in English",
    "fr": "Description en français",
    "default_translation": "This text will be applied to de and it"
}
```

## Example Response
Following the example above, a subsequent GET request would return a value for every supported language (the `default_translation` key is never returned):

```json
"description": {
    "en": "Description in English",
    "fr": "Description en français",
    "de": "This text will be applied to de and it",
    "it": "This text will be applied to de and it"
}
```

tags.name: Markdown
tags.description:
Some fields in this API (notably entity descriptions) accept Markdown formatting. ## Supported Formatting Only a subset of Markdown syntax is allowed; anything else is stripped out (sanitized). The accepted markup is: - **bold** via `**` or `__` - *italic* via `*` or `_` - underline via the HTML tag `` - ordered lists via `1.`, `2.`, `3.`, etc. - unordered lists via `*` or `-` The HTML tags matching these styles are also accepted, but they are converted to their Markdown equivalent: `` and `` become `**`, `` and `` become `_`, `
    `/`
      `/`
    1. ` become list markers. The only exception is ``, which is kept as-is since Markdown has no underline syntax. Any other tag is removed. Its text content is generally kept (e.g. a link `` is unwrapped but its label remains), but in some cases the content may be dropped as well. For this reason, you should only send the accepted markup and avoid any other HTML tag, as its rendering is not guaranteed. We recommend sanitizing your input on your side before submitting it, rather than relying on this endpoint to clean it up for you. ## Normalization Be aware that the content is reworked to be consistent, so what you get back may differ from what you submitted: - unordered list markers `*` are converted to `-` - bold `__` is normalized to `**` - italic `*` is normalized to `_` ## Example A request sending the following value: ```json "description": "Important: review the *checklist* below * first item * second item" ``` would be stored and returned in its normalized form: ```json "description": "**Important**: review the _checklist_ below - first item - second item" ```

tags.name: Event Timelines Fields
tags.description:
Some data is stored in an event timeline (i.e. history of changes) such as location, position, daily cost or currency exchange rate.
This allows in-app reporting to use accurate data at any point in time.

## General Information about timelines

A timeline is a list of events with the following fields:
- `value`: the value of the field at the time of the event and valid until the start of the next event
- `application_date`: the date at which the event starts (format YYYY-MM-DD or literal "first_event").

Every timeline must have a starting event ('application_date' = 'first_event') that represents the value to use before any other event.
If a user's field value has never been modified, the timeline will contain only the first event (which will act as the default value).
Order of events in the list is not important, the API will sort them by 'application_date' before processing ('first_event' first).
Events may be in the future, in which case the value is not yet applied (but will be taken into account by the in-app reporting)

'event_timelines' is a full-overwrite field, meaning that if you send a timeline, it will replace the existing one.
When dealing with timelines, the easiest way to update them is to retrieve the user data, modify the timeline and send it back.
For event reschedule, simply update the 'application_date' of the event you want to reschedule and send back the timeline.

## Specific Information about user event timelines

For user data, any in-app change or API call that modifies historicized user's data will update the event timeline of this user. This allows update the history automatically.

It is also possible to update the event timeline directly through the API while updating the field value.

Each historicized field has its own event timeline. All timelines can be accessed through the user endpoint, on the field 'event_timelines'.
Currently historicized fields are:
- location
- position
- business_unit
- daily_cost_info
- productive_share
- hours_per_day
- in_contract

While all the timelines are sent when retrieving a user data, it is not mandatory to send all timelines when updating a user.
You can send only the timeline(s) you want to update.

When sending a user event timeline, the event that is applicable at the current date MUST be compatible with the user's data AFTER the request is applied.
For example, the value of the current event for the location timeline should be the same as the user's location sent in the update/create request.
Or the same as the current user's location if no location is sent in the update request.

## Example with location change
Given a user with the following historic:
- first_event: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Developer, daily_cost = 500 €, productive_share = 0.8, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = False
- 2024-01-01: location = London, business_unit = BU_2, position = Developer Senior, daily_cost = 750 €, productive_share = 0.9, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True

If we want to change the user's information with the following updates:
- first event's location from Paris to Lyon
- application date of the location London from 2024-01-01 to 2025-01-01

The timeline to send would be:
```json
event_timelines: {
    "location": [
        {"application_date": "first_event", "value": "Lyon"},
        {"application_date": "2025-01-01", "value": "London"}
    ]
}
```

Then the user's data will be:
- first_event: location = Lyon, business_unit = BU_1, position = Developer, daily_cost = 500 €, productive_share = 0.8, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = False
- 2024-01-01: location = Lyon, business_unit = BU_2, position = Developer Senior, daily_cost = 750 €, productive_share = 0.9, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True
- 2025-01-01: location = London, business_unit = BU_2, position = Developer Senior, daily_cost = 750 €, productive_share = 0.9, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True

## Example with contract suspension
Given a user with the following historic:
- first_event: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Intern, daily_cost = 250 €, productive_share = 0.7, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = False
- 2024-01-01: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Intern, daily_cost = 250 €, productive_share = 0.7, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True

If we want to change the user's information with the following updates:
- user left as intern on 2024-06-30
- user was hired as full time contract on 2025-01-01

The timeline to send would be:
```json
event_timelines: {
    "in_contract": [
        {"application_date": "first_event", "value": false,
        {"application_date": "2024-01-01", "value": true},
        {"application_date": "2024-07-01", "value": false},
        {"application_date": "2025-01-01", "value": true}
    ],
    "position": [
        {"application_date": "first_event", "value": "Intern"},
        {"application_date": "2025-01-01", "value": "Developer"
}
```

Import note: The application_date of the event where the user is leaving is one day after the leaving_date to ensure that the user is still considered as "in contract" on their leaving date.

Then the user's data will be:
- first_event: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Intern, daily_cost = 500 €, productive_share = 0.8, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = False
- 2024-01-01: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Intern, daily_cost = 250 €, productive_share = 0.7, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True
- 2024-07-01: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Intern, daily_cost = 250 €, productive_share = 0.7, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = False
- 2025-01-01: location = Paris, business_unit = BU_1, position = Developer, daily_cost = 500 €, productive_share = 0.8, hours_per_day = 8.0, in_contract = True

## Summary
- Each timeline MUST contain at least one event
- Each timeline MUST contain EXACTLY one event with 'application_date' = 'first_event'

And for User Event Timelines :

- Send only the timelines you want to update
- The current event in each timeline MUST be compatible with the user's data after the request is applied

tags.name: Access Limitation Management
tags.description:
API Access can be limited to certain endpoints and/or methods (GET/PUT/DELETE).

Limitation can be set per access key so that different systems can have different access rights. For example:
- Access to only GET /users and PUT /users for the HR system (user synchronization)
- Access to only GET /time_entries and GET /projects (read-only access to access time entries)

Trying to access a forbidden endpoint or method will result in a 403 Forbidden error.

This feature is only available for Premium plan. Contact your Napta Account Manager in order to setup access limitations.

tags.name: Changes
tags.description:
## Policy
This API follows a policy of implementing non-breaking changes.
These changes aim to enhance functionality, improve performance,
or introduce new features without disrupting existing integrations.


If a change is considered breaking and incompatible with the current version,
it will be released in a new version to ensure continuity and stability for existing users.
In this spirit, a field may be deprecated (generally in favor of another one that replaces it): such a field
should no longer be used but remains fully functional. For backward compatibility reasons, it stays available and will not
be removed without a version bump of the Integration API, so you can keep relying on it.

More about the [API Backward Compatibility Policy](https://pickyourskills.slite.com/app/docs/jR9KMVV4cO6ZOF/API-Backward-Compatibility-Policy-shared)

## Changelog
This changelog provides a history of changes made to the API.


**October 2026:**
- Added support for the custom dropdown fields of Requests and Assignments, and of their periods, on /custom_dropdown_fields/<custom_key> endpoint: their values can now be retrieved, created and updated.

**September 2026:**
- New base URL `https://api.napta.io/integration/v1`. The previous base URL `https://api.napta.io/integration/v0` is deprecated: it exposes the exact same endpoints and behaviour and remains supported for backward compatibility, but should no longer be used.
- Added support for identifiers (napta_id or external_id) in the `custom_dropdown_fields` of `/assignments` endpoint and of its periods: on PUT, values can be given by identifier instead of name; on GET, the new query parameters `custom_dropdown_field[as]` (fields of the Assignment) and `periods.custom_dropdown_field[as]` (fields of its periods) return them as identifiers instead of names.
- Fixed the scope of `custom_dropdown_field[as]` on `GET /requests` endpoint: it now only applies to the custom dropdown fields of the Request itself. The ones of its periods, contributor_criteria and prebooked_users are identified separately with the new query parameters `periods.custom_dropdown_field[as]`, `contributor_criteria.custom_dropdown_field[as]` and `prebooked_users.custom_dropdown_field[as]` (default `name`).
- Added filter "status" on `GET /projects` endpoint, to filter projects on the name of their status, or on the absence of status (%00).
- Added filter "category" on `GET /projects` endpoint, to filter projects on the name of their category, or on the absence of category (%00).
- Added filter "archived" on `GET /projects` endpoint, to filter projects on whether they are archived or not.

**August 2026:**
- Improved the documentation.

**July 2026:**
- Improved the documentation.
- Fixed error 500 returned when trying to update a user with a hiring_date or leaving_date that is invalid regarding the current user's dates. Now returns an error 422 explaining to rather reset the other hiring/leaving_date or use the field user.event_timelines.in_contract to manage multi-contract periods.
- The referential endpoints (/clients, /business_units, /locations, /positions and /custom_dropdown_fields/<custom_key>) are now part of the standard documentation. They have been available since March 2026 but were previously only listed when browsing the documentation in advanced usage mode.

**June 2026:**
- Fixed the format of the `description` field on /skill_taxonomy/skills, /skill_taxonomy/certifications and /skill_taxonomy/grade_groups endpoints. The field now correctly accepts and returns Markdown (see [Markdown](#tag/Markdown)).
- Added subfield `custom_dropdown_fields` on field `contributor_criteria` of `/requests` endpoint. This allow to add a criterion upon which custom_dropdown_field is expected on the requested user.
- New /experiences endpoint with GET/PUT/DELETE methods.
- Added field `days_sold` on /requests endpoint.
- Added field `suggested_users` on /requests endpoint.
- Added field `prebooked_users` on /requests endpoint.
- Added fields `acquisition_date` and `expiry_date` on the PUT /certification_assessments endpoint and in the GET /certification_assessments endpoint response to manage the validity period of certifications.
- Added field `notes` on /time_entries endpoint. This allow to add more context about the time_entry.
- Added field `additional_visibility_on_business_units` on /users endpoint.
- Deprecated field `secondary_business_units` on /users endpoint, still supported for backward compatibility. Use `additional_visibility_on_business_units` instead.
- Added filter over endpoint /time_entries on projects (napta_id or external_id)

**May 2026:**
- Added field `event_timelines.custom_dropdown_fields` on /users endpoint to allow adding and modifying the historical values of custom_dropdown_fields of a user. Use technical keys from Admin > Dropdown fields (User Historised) as documentation keys are generic.
- New /certification_assessments endpoint with GET/PUT/DELETE methods.
- New /skill_taxonomy/skills endpoint with GET/PUT/DELETE methods.
- New /skill_taxonomy/certifications endpoint with GET/PUT/DELETE methods.
- New /skill_taxonomy/categories endpoint with GET/PUT/DELETE methods.
- New /skill_taxonomy/grade_groups endpoint with GET methods.
- Endpoint `/skill_assessments` is no longer in beta. Only skill assessments are now handled and returned; certification
assessments, which were previously included, are no longer part of the response.

**April 2026:**
- Added field `additional_staffing_rights_on_business_units` on /users endpoint to allow modifying/retrieving additional business units a user has staffing rights on.

**March 2026:**
- New /business_units endpoint with GET/PUT methods.
- New /clients endpoint with GET/PUT methods.
- New /custom_dropdown_fields/<custom_key> endpoint with GET/PUT methods.
- New /locations endpoint with GET/PUT methods.
- New /positions endpoint with GET/PUT methods.
- Added filter over Time Entries to filter on approval status (approved, pending, rejected) on GET /time_entries endpoint.

**February 2026:**
- Fixed a bug where assignment workload as rate was not correctly calculated when holidays existed in the period.

**January 2026:**
- Added support for hours and rates in /assignment and /request endpoints

**December 2025:**
- Added field `event_timelines.in_contract` on /users endpoint to allow adding and modifying contract suspensions of a user and its historic.
This introduces the ability to mark periods where a user is not in contract (internship, sabbatical, leave without pay, etc).
The feature will be progressively rolled out to all clients over the months of December and January.
In the meantime, trying to set this field may result in a 422 Unprocessable Entity error.
- Field `description` on /projects and /users endpoints now accepts empty string. Empty strings are treated as null (clears the description).

**October 2025:**
- Added field `activity_description` on /assignments and /requests endpoints. Allow to give more details about the task to be done, the expected profile and the requirements.

It is either the `daily_fee_info` if set, or the user's default daily_fee at the start date of the assignment period or null if no user default daily fee is set.

tags.name: Managing referential objects
tags.description:
The API lets you easily reference other objects using their name. But this has some limitations when it comes to managing a referential that may evolve over time (in particular when you need to update the name of an object).


In order to manage a referential, you may access to dedicated endpoints (see [Endpoints - Referential objects](#tag/Endpoints---Referential-objects) section)


When creating or updating an object, you can reference objects of the referential by their name (simple use case) OR by their identifier using a dictionary with either `napta_id` or `external_id` (advanced use case).


When retrieving data, you may use query parameters to choose to have referential objects represented by their name (simple use case) OR by their identifier (advanced use case). For example, to retrieve the Client of a Projects as an identifier, use the query parameter `?client[as]=identifier`

tags.name: User
tags.description:
User related endpoints.


User deletion is not supported by the API as it will result in data loss on several relations and will impact reportings.
However you can deactivate the user instead.

tags.name: Project
tags.description: Project related endpoints.

tags.name: Time Entry
tags.description:
Time Entry related endpoints.


A time entry is a time imputation of a user on a project for a date.

tags.name: Leave
tags.description:
Leave related endpoints.


A Leave is a period of time during which a user is not working.

It is represented by a start date and an end date.

Half-days are supported through starts_at_midday and ends_at_midday parameters.

tags.name: Assignment
tags.description:
Assignment related endpoints.


An Assignment represents a staffing need on a project that **has been assigned to a User**.

**Lifecycle**
- If a User is unassigned from an Assignment, the Assignment transitions back into a [Request](#tag/Request).
- You cannot assign or unassign Users through the API — this action is only possible through the App interface.

**Limitations**
- The [external_id](#tag/External-Ids) must be unique across Requests and Assignments, as a Request can transition into Assignments and vice versa.
- Assignments on project snapshots cannot be retrieved or modified.

tags.name: Request
tags.description:
Request related endpoints.


A Request represents a staffing need on a project that **has not yet been assigned to a User**.

**Lifecycle**
- If a User is assigned on a Request, the Request transitions into an [Assignment](#tag/Assignment).
- You cannot assign or unassign Users through the API — this action is only possible through the App interface.

**Limitations**
- The [external_id](#tag/External-Ids) must be unique across Requests and Assignments, as a Request can transition into Assignments.
- Requests on project snapshots cannot be retrieved or modified.

tags.name: Currency
tags.description:
Currency related endpoints.


Currencies allows to manage different currencies with different exchange rate.
One currency on the app is considered as the main currency, it is the currency used as reference for all exchange rates. This is set by Napta and cannot be changed.
Exchange rates can be set for a specific period of time and are used in the app for all financial calculations.
A currency may be archived (except the main currency) to prevent its use in the app (old values will still be visible).

tags.name: Skill Assessment
tags.description:
Skill Assessment related endpoints.


Skill Assessments allow to evaluate the skills of users in different areas.

tags.name: Certification Assessment
tags.description:
Certification assessment related endpoints.


Certification assessments allow to evaluate the certifications of users in different areas.

tags.name: Experience
tags.description:
Experience related endpoints.


An Experience represents a past professional engagement in a User's career history.

tags.name: Grade Group
tags.description:
Grade Group of Skills related endpoints.


Grade Groups define the standardized evaluation scales used to measure proficiency across the application.
A Grade Group consists of a set of levels (grades) that provide a consistent framework for assessment.
Once defined, these groups are assigned to specific skills or certifications to ensure that every evaluation follows a pre-established and uniform grading logic.


Grade groups can be created and managed through the Napta App [here](https://app.napta.io/admin/grade_group).

tags.name: Category
tags.description:
Category related endpoints.


Categories define different areas or types of competencies and are shared between skills and certifications.
They allow you to organize skills and certifications into logical groups (e.g., "Technical Skills", "Soft Skills", "Languages").
This hierarchical organization is essential for navigating the referential and building a coherent mapping of the company's expertise.

tags.name: Skill
tags.description:
Skills related endpoints.


Skills represent the individual competencies present within your company.
Every skill must be linked to a Category for organizational purposes and associated with a Grade Group to define its grading scale.
This dual association ensures that each skill is correctly classified in the referential and consistently assessed across employees.

tags.name: Certification
tags.description:
Certifications related endpoints.


Certifications represent the formal qualifications recognized within your company.
Every certification must be linked to a Category for organizational purposes and associated with a Grade Group to define its grading scale.
This dual association ensures that each certification is correctly classified in the referential and consistently tracked across employees.

tags.name: Client
tags.description:
Client related endpoints.


A Client represents a company or an organization that you are working for or with.
It is used as a categorization field for projects.

tags.name: Business Unit
tags.description:
Business Unit related endpoints.


A Business Unit represents a department or a division in your organization.

tags.name: Location
tags.description:
Location related endpoints.


A Location represents a physical place where your employees are working.

tags.name: Position
tags.description:
Position related endpoints.


A Position represents a role or a job title in your organization.

tags.name: Custom Dropdown Field
tags.description:
Custom Dropdown Field related endpoints.


These endpoints allow to retrieve, create and update possible values of Custom Dropdown Field.

Manageable Custom Dropdown Fields are the ones of Projects, Users (including historised ones), Requests and Assignments, and of the periods of Requests and Assignments.

Custom Dropdown Field can't be creating using the API and must be created on the platform administration panel.

You can find all Custom Dropdown Field and their associated unique key from the administration panel.


See [Custom Dropdown Fields](#tag/Custom-Fields/Custom-Dropdown-Fields) for more information.
